name: VFF Early Phase Financing (Vroegefasefinanciering)
summary: A loan for innovative Dutch companies at proof-of-principle stage that aim for a proof of concept and have a follow-up investor lined up. It is repaid with interest.
amount: Up to EUR 450,000 loan at 7.71 percent interest (rate from 1 Sep 2026)
next_steps: Confirm on the official page whether a sole trader can apply (the page speaks of a company)
Do the free RVO Quick Scan
Secure an investor who will come in after the project

name: Innovatiekrediet
summary: A repayable credit for technical development with a high risk of failure, for innovative companies that can reach the market within 5 years. Repayment is due only on success.
amount: Up to 45 percent of project costs for small companies (35 percent medium, 25 percent large; up to 50 percent for small and medium companies in collaborations)

deadline.note: Applications open all year; the 2026 funding period ends 31 Dec 2026, the 2027 period is not yet confirmed

next_steps: Confirm the Dutch establishment rule on the official page
Show at least 55 percent of project costs funded from other sources
Prepare a technical risk and market plan (market within 5 years)

name: WBSO (R&D wage tax reduction and self-employed deduction)
provider: Netherlands Enterprise Agency (RVO), Dutch Tax Administration
summary: A tax reduction for developing new software or technical research in the Netherlands. Self-employed people get a fixed R&D deduction; businesses with staff get a wage tax reduction.
amount: 2026: 36 percent wage tax reduction on the first EUR 391,020 of R&D cost (50 percent for starters), 16 percent above; self-employed deduction EUR 15,979 plus EUR 7,996 for starters

deadline.note: Apply in advance for future R&D work; 2027 applications open from mid-November 2026

next_steps: Register with the Dutch business register and taxes so the business pays income tax
Log in with eHerkenning (level 3) and write the project plan in advance
Plan the work in phases with a technical problem to solve

name: Innovation Box (Innovatiebox)
summary: A reduced corporate tax rate on profit from innovation that RVO has declared as R&D (S&O-verklaring). It applies to corporate income tax, not to a sole trader's income tax.
amount: 9 percent effective corporate tax rate on qualifying profit
next_steps: Only useful once a Dutch BV makes profit from the declared innovation
Obtain the RVO S&O declaration (through WBSO) for the innovation
Ask an adviser to confirm the rules for your situation

name: YES!Delft Validation and Accelerator
summary: Delft incubator with Validation and Accelerator programs; the Accelerator is described as operating without taking equity. Requirements: at least two co-founders, a clear idea, innovative technology, and a base in or plan to move to the Netherlands (solo founders must first join the Meet your co-founder workshop). Duration, fee and dates not stated.
amount: No equity taken in the Accelerator
next_steps: Book a call with the Investment Director
Join the Meet your co-founder workshop if solo
Plan a Netherlands base

name: Rockstart
summary: Invests from pre-seed to Series B in AgriFood, Energy and Emerging Tech with mentor-driven support and fundraising preparation; offices in Amsterdam, Copenhagen and Bogota. Also corporate programs (Orsted Propel, New Energy Challenge). Amounts, equity and deadlines not stated on the page.
next_steps: Use the Get started form
Check which sector track fits
Confirm terms

name: PLNT startup programs
summary: Programs including Ready to Start (launching a science-based startup), Startup Play (assess an idea), Venture Academy (prepare for market launch), unlock_ (life sciences and health sector), Sprout (coaching), and Ready to Impact (The Hague). Costs, equity and the location of each program are not stated; there is a quiz to pick a program.
next_steps: Take the program quiz on the site
Check the page of the matching program
Ask PLNT about cost

name: Borgstelling MKB-kredieten (BMKB)
provider: Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland (RVO), Ministry of Economic Affairs
summary: State guarantee on a bank loan for Dutch SMEs that lack collateral; sole proprietorships and partnerships can use it.
amount: Loans up to EUR 1.5 million; state guarantees 90% of the credit, covering up to three quarters of financing up to EUR 333,333 and up to half above that

deadline.note: Expanded scheme runs through 1 July 2027; apply via your financier, not RVO

next_steps: Check the business has up to 250 FTE and turnover up to EUR 50 million or balance sheet up to EUR 43 million
Ask your bank or an accredited financier whether BMKB fits
Compare the green variant BMKB-G for sustainability investments

name: DHI subsidy: demonstration, feasibility and investment preparation
summary: Subsidy for Dutch SMEs with international ambitions for demonstration projects, feasibility studies and investment preparation projects abroad.
amount: 50% or 70% of costs: demonstration up to EUR 200,000; feasibility study up to EUR 100,000; investment preparation up to EUR 100,000; 2026 budget EUR 8.5 million

deadline.note: Open 2 March to 31 December 2026 while budget lasts; only one DHI project in progress at a time

next_steps: Submit the quickscan first, then follow the Stappenplan
Check the full eligibility conditions on the RVO page
Apply early because budget is limited

name: Support International Business (SIB) subsidy
summary: Small subsidies for market entry, export training and coaching, knowledge and skills, trade fairs and trade missions.
amount: 50% to 80% of costs, up to EUR 2,500 per activity (coaching up to EUR 1,000; trade mission up to EUR 1,500)

deadline.note: 2026 budget is exhausted; new funding from January 2027

next_steps: Check the eligibility conditions in the regulation linked from the RVO page
Plan activities for 2027 and apply when funding reopens
Contact RVO advisors for eligibility questions

name: Innovation Impact Challenge (formerly SBIR)
provider: Rijksdienst voor Ondernemend Nederland (RVO) for Dutch government bodies
summary: Phased innovation competition where government pays companies to test and develop solutions to public challenges. Phase 1 is a feasibility study, phase 2 development; the company keeps its IP.
amount: Payment equals the approved offer, below a maximum set per challenge; See the official page for the current round

deadline.note: Challenges open at different times; check the Oproepen section for current calls

next_steps: Open the Oproepen section for current challenges
Read the challenge documents on the Offertes indienen page
Submit an offer within the stated maximum

name: Qredits business loans for entrepreneurs
summary: Microfinance for Dutch entrepreneurs, including established ones taking over a business, investing in assets, hiring staff or making sustainability changes. Includes a free coach and training.
amount: See the official page for the current round (Qredits reports EUR 927 million lent across 42,030 loans)

deadline.note: Apply online; Qredits then holds a personal conversation

next_steps: Apply online on qredits.nl
Prepare for the personal conversation about your situation
Ask for the free coach and training with the loan

name: Dutch Student Investment Fund (DSIF)
summary: Student-run fund investing in startups of University of Twente or Saxion students and recent graduates; the company should be built in Overijssel.

deadline.note: No deadlines; contact at any stage

next_steps: Confirm you are a student, PhD or recent graduate of Twente or Saxion
Send a one-pager through the Apply for funding page
Prepare a business plan and a board pitch

name: Graduate Entrepreneur Fund (Pre-Seed)
provider: Delft University Fund and Graduate platform
summary: Pre-seed fund for startups founded by TU Delft alumni, students or staff. The Graduate platform serves students and young alumni of TU Delft, Erasmus University Rotterdam and Erasmus MC. The page is written for donors, so check graduate.nl for founder terms.
amount: Initial investment of up to EUR 100,000; about 20 to 30 startups a year

deadline.note: No dates on the page. See the official page for the current round

next_steps: Check eligibility on graduate.nl
Contact the Graduate team at hello@Graduate.nl
Confirm the terms before applying

name: Graduate Ventures
summary: Dutch university-linked fund investing at pre-seed and seed. The page shows partner university logos that appear to include Leiden and LUMC but does not state who may apply.
amount: Invests up to EUR 3 million in pre-seed and seed founders

deadline.note: No intake dates on the page. See the official page for the current round

next_steps: Read the Explore funding page on graduate.nl
Email hello@Graduate.nl to confirm whether Leiden students and alumni qualify
Prepare a short pitch

name: Invest-NL
summary: Dutch government-backed investor acting as co-financier for innovative companies and projects in carbon-neutral and circular economy, sustainable food, affordable healthcare and deep tech, targeting businesses that will need at least EUR 10 million in financing. Start with the online financieringscheck.
next_steps: Complete the Invest-NL financieringscheck
Confirm your total financing need is at least EUR 10 million
Use the contact page to reach the team if the check is positive

name: InnovationQuarter
summary: South Holland regional development agency with over EUR 300 million in fund capital (including UNIIQ and InnovationQuarter Capital). Apply with the online quickscan or by phone or email. Aimed at technology startups and scale-ups based in or affecting Zuid-Holland, including Leiden.
amount: Typically EUR 250,000 to EUR 5,000,000, often as part of a round with co-investors
next_steps: Take the 5 minute quickscan on the funding page
Complete the intake form
Confirm you are based in or impact Zuid-Holland

name: UNIIQ
summary: EUR 50 million early-stage fund for research-driven startups with complex technology, often university spin-offs in life sciences and deeptech. Gives startup capital as a convertible loan plus hands-on support. Book a free orientation conversation; no application fee is mentioned.

deadline.note: Free orientation sessions; no deadline stated

next_steps: Book a free orientation conversation through the spreekuren page
Prepare a short description of the technology and team
Ask about the investment process and Vroege Fase Financiering

name: Invesdor (formerly Oneplanetcrowd)
summary: Equity and bond crowdfunding platform licensed under the EU ECSP crowdfunding regulation (licence covers Germany, Austria, Scandinavia and the Benelux). Apply through the online form. The page lists no application fee.
amount: EUR 250,000 to EUR 5 million (the page also gives EUR 500,000 as the lower bound in one place)

deadline.note: Apply any time; campaigns run up to three weeks

next_steps: Submit the form on the Invesdor business financing page
Confirm fees in the mandate agreement before signing
Prepare for due diligence and legal documents
